obtained.how: not obtained: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society (now OUP / Taylor & Francis), subscription; no open copy found

bibliography.note: Whitledge, G. W., Hayward, R. S., Zweifel, R. D. & Rabeni, C. F., Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 132(2): 316–325 (March 2003), title as cited

claims.claim: the set's respiration was measured only at 18–30 °C, on Missouri fish (via Brownscombe, Smith & Bzonek 2024)
its weight exponent is RB −0.756, about three times the usual slope
claims.note: the value as stored in FB4's parameter file was checked under Deslauriers_etal_2017 (Parameters_official.csv, Whitledge rows: RA 0.244, RB −0.756); not checked against Whitledge et al.'s own table

claims.claim: negative energy budget at maximum ration for a 5-g fish at every temperature; break-even ~10 g at 20 °C and 20–25 g at 15 and 25 °C; usable only above ~30 g (project arithmetic)
claims.note: project arithmetic on the FB4-stored set; see Deslauriers_etal_2017's evidence for the FB4 inputs

claims.claim: the set is published as two rows by temperature: CQ 4.2 at ≤ 26 °C, 1.95 above (with CA 0.339, CB −0.31, CTO 22, CTM 37, RA 0.244, RQ 1.8, RTO 30, RTM 37, SDA 0.15848, FA 0.104, UA 0.0882)
smallmouth bass run on the Whitledge et al. 2003 set (with the Rice et al. 1983 largemouth set below 250 g)
claims.note: the 250-g switch is stageR5's (src/w3/fish3.js:632); species.js's default juvW is 30 g — the table describes the package run, which is fine if the text says so

tried.note: only a university-proxy copy (webvpn) — behind a login, not used

notes: For the human to fetch: doi:10.1577/1548-8659(2003)132<0316:DALEOA>2.0.CO;2. When read, check the temperature range of the respiration trials (18–30 °C is quoted via Brownscombe et al. 2024), the fish's origin and size range (the abstract, per a search snippet, evaluated fish of 100–270 g), and whether the two-row CQ (≤ 26 °C / > 26 °C) is Whitledge's or FB4's arrangement.
